37: func Parse(filename string, input []byte) ([]ServerBlock, error) {

39: 	// remain a read-only operation, but we have to expand environment
40: 	// variables before we parse, which changes the underlying array (#4422)
41: 	inputCopy := make([]byte, len(input))
42: 	copy(inputCopy, input)
43: 
44: 	tokens, err := allTokens(filename, inputCopy)
45: 	if err != nil {
46: 		return nil, err
47: 	}
48: 	p := parser{
49: 		Dispenser: NewDispenser(tokens),
50: 		importGraph: importGraph{
51: 			nodes: make(map[string]bool),
52: 			edges: make(adjacency),
53: 		},
54: 	}
55: 	return p.parseAll()

60: // and in order. It may mutate input as it expands env vars.

105: func (p *parser) begin() error {

107: 		return nil
108: 	}

112: 		return err
113: 	}
114: 
115: 	if p.eof {
116: 		// this happens if the Caddyfile consists of only
117: 		// a line of addresses and nothing else

119: 	}

121: 	if ok, name := p.isNamedRoute(); ok {
122: 		// named routes only have one key, the route name
123: 		p.block.Keys = []string{name}
124: 		p.block.IsNamedRoute = true
125: 
126: 		// we just need a dummy leading token to ease parsing later
127: 		nameToken := p.Token()
128: 		nameToken.Text = name
129: 
130: 		// get all the tokens from the block, including the braces
131: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(true)
132: 		if err != nil {
133: 			return err
134: 		}
135: 		tokens = append([]Token{nameToken}, tokens...)
136: 		p.block.Segments = []Segment{tokens}

138: 	}

140: 	if ok, name := p.isSnippet(); ok {
141: 		if p.definedSnippets == nil {
142: 			p.definedSnippets = map[string][]Token{}
143: 		}
144: 		if _, found := p.definedSnippets[name]; found {
145: 			return p.Errf("redeclaration of previously declared snippet %s", name)
146: 		}

148: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(false)
149: 		if err != nil {

151: 		}
152: 		// Just as we need to track which file the token comes from, we need to
153: 		// keep track of which snippet the token comes from. This is helpful
154: 		// in tracking import cycles across files/snippets by namespacing them.

156: 		for k, v := range tokens {
157: 			v.snippetName = name

160: 		p.definedSnippets[name] = tokens

162: 		p.block.Keys = nil

169: func (p *parser) addresses() error {
170: 	var expectingAnother bool
171: 
172: 	for {
173: 		tkn := p.Val()
174: 
175: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
176: 		if tkn == "import" && p.isNewLine() {
177: 			err := p.doImport(0)
178: 			if err != nil {
179: 				return err
180: 			}
181: 			continue
182: 		}
183: 
184: 		// Open brace definitely indicates end of addresses
185: 		if tkn == "{" {
186: 			if expectingAnother {
187: 				return p.Errf("Expected another address but had '%s' - check for extra comma", tkn)
188: 			}
189: 			// Mark this server block as being defined with braces.
190: 			// This is used to provide a better error message when
191: 			// the user may have tried to define two server blocks
192: 			// without having used braces, which are required in
193: 			// that case.
194: 			p.block.HasBraces = true
195: 			break
196: 		}
197: 
198: 		// Users commonly forget to place a space between the address and the '{'
199: 		if strings.HasSuffix(tkn, "{") {
200: 			return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot end with a curly brace: '%s' - put a space between the token and the brace", tkn)
201: 		}
202: 
203: 		if tkn != "" { // empty token possible if user typed ""
204: 			// Trailing comma indicates another address will follow, which
205: 			// may possibly be on the next line
206: 			if tkn[len(tkn)-1] == ',' {
207: 				tkn = tkn[:len(tkn)-1]
208: 				expectingAnother = true
209: 			} else {
210: 				expectingAnother = false // but we may still see another one on this line
211: 			}
212: 
213: 			// If there's a comma here, it's probably because they didn't use a space
214: 			// between their two domains, e.g. "foo.com,bar.com", which would not be
215: 			// parsed as two separate site addresses.
216: 			if strings.Contains(tkn, ",") {
217: 				return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot contain a comma ',': '%s' - put a space after the comma to separate site addresses", tkn)
218: 			}

220: 			p.block.Keys = append(p.block.Keys, tkn)
221: 		}
222: 
223: 		// Advance token and possibly break out of loop or return error
224: 		hasNext := p.Next()
225: 		if expectingAnother && !hasNext {
226: 			return p.EOFErr()
227: 		}
228: 		if !hasNext {
229: 			p.eof = true
230: 			break // EOF
231: 		}
232: 		if !expectingAnother && p.isNewLine() {
233: 			break
234: 		}
235: 	}
236: 
237: 	return nil

263: // directives parses through all the lines for directives
264: // and it expects the next token to be the first
265: // directive. It goes until EOF or closing curly brace
266: // which ends the server block.
267: func (p *parser) directives() error {
268: 	for p.Next() {
269: 		// end of server block
270: 		if p.Val() == "}" {
271: 			// p.nesting has already been decremented
272: 			break
273: 		}
274: 
275: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
276: 		if p.Val() == "import" {
277: 			err := p.doImport(1)
278: 			if err != nil {
279: 				return err
280: 			}
281: 			p.cursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
282: 			continue
283: 		}
284: 
285: 		// normal case: parse a directive as a new segment
286: 		// (a "segment" is a line which starts with a directive
287: 		// and which ends at the end of the line or at the end of
288: 		// the block that is opened at the end of the line)
289: 		if err := p.directive(); err != nil {
290: 			return err
291: 		}
292: 	}

297: // doImport swaps out the import directive and its argument
298: // (a total of 2 tokens) with the tokens in the specified file
299: // or globbing pattern. When the function returns, the cursor
300: // is on the token before where the import directive was. In
301: // other words, call Next() to access the first token that was
302: // imported.
303: func (p *parser) doImport(nesting int) error {
304: 	// syntax checks
305: 	if !p.NextArg() {
306: 		return p.ArgErr()
307: 	}
308: 	importPattern := p.Val()
309: 	if importPattern == "" {
310: 		return p.Err("Import requires a non-empty filepath")
311: 	}
312: 
313: 	// grab remaining args as placeholder replacements
314: 	args := p.RemainingArgs()
315: 
316: 	// set up a replacer for non-variadic args replacement
317: 	repl := makeArgsReplacer(args)
318: 
319: 	// splice out the import directive and its arguments
320: 	// (2 tokens, plus the length of args)
321: 	tokensBefore := p.tokens[:p.cursor-1-len(args)]
322: 	tokensAfter := p.tokens[p.cursor+1:]
323: 	var importedTokens []Token
324: 	var nodes []string
325: 
326: 	// first check snippets. That is a simple, non-recursive replacement
327: 	if p.definedSnippets != nil && p.definedSnippets[importPattern] != nil {
328: 		importedTokens = p.definedSnippets[importPattern]
329: 		if len(importedTokens) > 0 {
330: 			// just grab the first one
331: 			nodes = append(nodes, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", importedTokens[0].File, importedTokens[0].snippetName))
332: 		}
333: 	} else {
334: 		// make path relative to the file of the _token_ being processed rather
335: 		// than current working directory (issue #867) and then use glob to get
336: 		// list of matching filenames
337: 		absFile, err := filepath.Abs(p.Dispenser.File())
338: 		if err != nil {
339: 			return p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", p.Dispenser.File(), err)
340: 		}
341: 
342: 		var matches []string
343: 		var globPattern string
344: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(importPattern) {
345: 			globPattern = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(absFile), importPattern)
346: 		} else {
347: 			globPattern = importPattern
348: 		}
349: 		if strings.Count(globPattern, "*") > 1 || strings.Count(globPattern, "?") > 1 ||
350: 			(strings.Contains(globPattern, "[") && strings.Contains(globPattern, "]")) {
351: 			// See issue #2096 - a pattern with many glob expansions can hang for too long
352: 			return p.Errf("Glob pattern may only contain one wildcard (*), but has others: %s", globPattern)
353: 		}
354: 		matches, err = filepath.Glob(globPattern)
355: 
356: 		if err != nil {
357: 			return p.Errf("Failed to use import pattern %s: %v", importPattern, err)
358: 		}
359: 		if len(matches) == 0 {
360: 			if strings.ContainsAny(globPattern, "*?[]") {
361: 				caddy.Log().Warn("No files matching import glob pattern", zap.String("pattern", importPattern))
362: 			} else {
363: 				return p.Errf("File to import not found: %s", importPattern)
364: 			}
365: 		} else {
366: 			// See issue #5295 - should skip any files that start with a . when iterating over them.
367: 			sep := string(filepath.Separator)
368: 			segGlobPattern := strings.Split(globPattern, sep)
369: 			if strings.HasPrefix(segGlobPattern[len(segGlobPattern)-1], "*") {

371: 				for _, m := range matches {
372: 					seg := strings.Split(m, sep)
373: 					if !strings.HasPrefix(seg[len(seg)-1], ".") {
374: 						tmpMatches = append(tmpMatches, m)
375: 					}
376: 				}
377: 				matches = tmpMatches
378: 			}
379: 		}
380: 
381: 		// collect all the imported tokens
382: 		for _, importFile := range matches {
383: 			newTokens, err := p.doSingleImport(importFile)
384: 			if err != nil {
385: 				return err
386: 			}
387: 			importedTokens = append(importedTokens, newTokens...)
388: 		}
389: 		nodes = matches
390: 	}
391: 
392: 	nodeName := p.File()
393: 	if p.Token().snippetName != "" {
394: 		nodeName += fmt.Sprintf(":%s", p.Token().snippetName)
395: 	}
396: 	p.importGraph.addNode(nodeName)

401: 	}

403: 	// copy the tokens so we don't overwrite p.definedSnippets
404: 	tokensCopy := make([]Token, 0, len(importedTokens))
405: 
406: 	var (
407: 		maybeSnippet   bool
408: 		maybeSnippetId bool
409: 		index          int
410: 	)

412: 	// run the argument replacer on the tokens
413: 	// golang for range slice return a copy of value
414: 	// similarly, append also copy value
415: 	for i, token := range importedTokens {
416: 		// update the token's imports to refer to import directive filename, line number and snippet name if there is one
417: 		if token.snippetName != "" {

429: 			} else {

431: 			}

433: 			if index == 0 && len(token.Text) >= 3 && strings.HasPrefix(token.Text, "(") && strings.HasSuffix(token.Text, ")") {
434: 				maybeSnippetId = true
435: 			}
436: 		}
437: 
438: 		switch token.Text {

445: 		case "}":

447: 			if nesting == 0 && maybeSnippet {
448: 				maybeSnippet = false
449: 			}
450: 		}

452: 		if maybeSnippet {

457: 		foundVariadic, startIndex, endIndex := parseVariadic(token, len(args))

463: 		} else {

465: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)

467: 	}

470: 	// and rewind cursor so Next() will land on first imported token
471: 	p.tokens = append(tokensBefore, append(tokensCopy, tokensAfter...)...)

477: // doSingleImport lexes the individual file at importFile and returns
478: // its tokens or an error, if any.
479: func (p *parser) doSingleImport(importFile string) ([]Token, error) {
480: 	file, err := os.Open(importFile)
481: 	if err != nil {
482: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
483: 	}
484: 	defer file.Close()
485: 
486: 	if info, err := file.Stat(); err != nil {
487: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
488: 	} else if info.IsDir() {
489: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: is a directory", importFile)
490: 	}
491: 
492: 	input, err := io.ReadAll(file)
493: 	if err != nil {
494: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read imported file %s: %v", importFile, err)
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	// only warning in case of empty files
498: 	if len(input) == 0 || len(strings.TrimSpace(string(input))) == 0 {
499: 		caddy.Log().Warn("Import file is empty", zap.String("file", importFile))
500: 		return []Token{}, nil
501: 	}
502: 
503: 	importedTokens, err := allTokens(importFile, input)
504: 	if err != nil {
505: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read tokens while importing %s: %v", importFile, err)
506: 	}
507: 
508: 	// Tack the file path onto these tokens so errors show the imported file's name
509: 	// (we use full, absolute path to avoid bugs: issue #1892)
510: 	filename, err := filepath.Abs(importFile)
511: 	if err != nil {
512: 		return nil, p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", importFile, err)
513: 	}
514: 	for i := 0; i < len(importedTokens); i++ {
515: 		importedTokens[i].File = filename
516: 	}
517: 
518: 	return importedTokens, nil
519: }

521: // directive collects tokens until the directive's scope
522: // closes (either end of line or end of curly brace block).
523: // It expects the currently-loaded token to be a directive
524: // (or } that ends a server block). The collected tokens
525: // are loaded into the current server block for later use
526: // by directive setup functions.
527: func (p *parser) directive() error {
528: 
529: 	// a segment is a list of tokens associated with this directive
530: 	var segment Segment
531: 
532: 	// the directive itself is appended as a relevant token
533: 	segment = append(segment, p.Token())
534: 
535: 	for p.Next() {
536: 		if p.Val() == "{" {
537: 			p.nesting++
538: 			if !p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
539: 				return p.Err("Unexpected next token after '{' on same line")
540: 			}
541: 			if p.isNewLine() {
542: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{' on a new line; did you mean to place the '{' on the previous line?")
543: 			}
544: 		} else if p.Val() == "{}" {
545: 			if p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
546: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{}' at end of line")
547: 			}
548: 		} else if p.isNewLine() && p.nesting == 0 {
549: 			p.cursor-- // read too far
550: 			break
551: 		} else if p.Val() == "}" && p.nesting > 0 {
552: 			p.nesting--
